reason: picomatch <= 4.0.7 has no patched release; it backtracks exponentially only when the glob PATTERN it compiles is a single-branch repeated extglob such as +(*). Here it is reached only from web/ (tools/apigen does not install it), at 4.0.7, as a dev-only package (web/package-lock.json marks it dev) pulled in by vite, vitest and tinyglobby, with fdir as a peer. The gate holds this entry to that graph: it waives the advisory only in web, and only while every node npm reports it on is dev in web/package-lock.json. It runs in the Vite dev server, vite build and vitest: on developer machines, in CI, and in the builder stage of docker/Dockerfile.web. Nothing deployed loads it: the web image ships nginx serving static dist/, and server, worker and migrate are Go binaries. The patterns it compiles are repo-authored or pinned: coverage include/exclude and the coverage threshold keys in web/vite.config.ts; the defaults of the lockfile-pinned vite and vitest (test include/exclude, server.fs.deny, watcher ignores, forceRerunTriggers) and the filters and glob rewrites of lockfile-pinned plugins and PostCSS; and the exports keys of lockfile-pinned dependencies; web/src has no import.meta.glob. Dev-server request paths are matched against those patterns as input and never compiled as one. No request, user or untrusted file supplies a pattern, and anyone able to change one already runs code in that process, so the worst case is a stalled local or CI build.
